# Which way will the top of the purple-and-pink balloon move?

## Short answer

**The top (crown) of the balloon will move upwards and to the left.** It will lift
off the grass and swing through roughly a quarter-turn — anticlockwise as we see it
in the photograph — until it is directly above the basket, which is off to the left
beyond the edge of the frame. It will also come slightly *towards* the camera as it
does so, because the basket end of the balloon is nearer to the viewer than the crown
currently is.

## Why — how the balloon is lying at the moment

The purple, pink, cream and dark-red balloon on the left is lying on its side on the
grass, part way through inflation. Reading the envelope from left to right:

- Its bulk fills the whole left-hand side of the picture and is cut off by the top
  and left edges of the frame. This is the fat middle ("equator") of the envelope,
  and it is the part closest to the camera.
- Moving to the right, the envelope steadily tapers. The horizontal ring tapes bunch
  closer and closer together and the vertical gore tapes converge.
- They all meet at a single gathered point roughly in the middle-left of the frame,
  just above the heads of the small group of people standing by the fabric. That
  gathered point is the **crown ring — the top of the balloon**. A thin crown line
  runs away from it across the sky to the right.
- Past the crown, the remaining fabric simply drapes loosely down to the grass, and
  there is no basket, no burner frame and no open throat anywhere at that end.

Because the basket and the mouth are nowhere to be seen in the picture, they must be
off the left-hand edge of the frame, at the near end of the envelope. So the balloon
is laid out with its **mouth/basket off-frame to the left and near the camera, and
its crown pointing to the right and away into the background**, towards the other
balloons.

## What happens as it fills with hot air

1. Hot air makes the envelope buoyant, so the crown end starts to float upwards off
   the ground.
2. The mouth end stays put on the ground, anchored by the basket and the crew, so the
   balloon pivots about that end like a hinge.
3. The crown therefore sweeps out an arc of about 90 degrees: it rises off the grass,
   travels **leftwards** across the picture (towards the left-hand edge, where the
   basket is) while climbing **upwards** into the sky.
4. The movement finishes with the crown vertically above the basket, the envelope
   standing tall and the balloon upright and ready to lift the basket off the ground.

## Stating the direction explicitly

- Horizontally, the top moves **to the left** in the image — away from the crowd and
  the other balloons, towards the out-of-frame basket.
- Vertically, the top moves **upwards**.
- In terms of rotation in the plane of the photograph, that is an **anticlockwise**
  (counter-clockwise) rotation of about 90 degrees.
- In depth, the top also moves slightly **towards the viewer**, since the pivot
  (the basket) is closer to the camera than the crown is now.

Combined: **up and to the left, arcing over the basket.**

Its long axis runs from the near left of the picture (the huge, rounded part of the envelope that fills the left edge of the frame and runs off-frame) toward the middle of the picture, where the envelope narrows to a point on the ground.

- The top of the balloon **rises off the ground (moves upward)** and at the same time **swings to the right**, toward the basket end at the centre of the picture (and slightly away from the camera, since the basket end is farther from the viewer).

- The motion stops when the crown is directly above the mouth and basket, i.e. the balloon standing upright over the spot where the crew are now holding the mouth, so the finished upright balloon will stand roughly where the narrow end currently touches the ground, near the middle of the photo.
